html:
The battle on 30 July 101 BCE, on the Raudine Plain near Vercellae in northern Italy, where Roman armies under Gaius Marius and Quintus Lutatius Catulus destroyed the Cimbri. It ended the Cimbrian War.

The Cimbri had crossed the Alps into the Po valley while Marius was finishing off the Teutons in Gaul. Their king Boiorix is said to have asked Marius to name a day and place for battle. The Romans, fighting with the sun and dust behind them, broke the Cimbri, and Boiorix was killed. Ancient writers say the Cimbri women killed their children and themselves rather than be taken. Many thousands of survivors were sold as slaves.

The army that won was the one Marius had rebuilt in the Marian reforms. Rome hailed him as its third founder, after Romulus and Camillus. Catulus and Marius quarrelled over who deserved the credit.
sum: The battle on 30 July 101 BCE, on the Raudine Plain near Vercellae in northern Italy, where Roman armies under Gaius Marius and Quintus Lutatius Catulus destroyed the Cimbri. It ended the Cimbrian War.
